value: Housing Act (Stanovanjski zakon, SZ-1), as summarised by the Ministry on the "Najemna razmerja" (rental relations) page.
source_publisher: Ministry of Natural Resources and Spatial Planning of Slovenia (PIS spatial information portal)
note: Official government guidance on the Housing Act (Stanovanjski zakon, SZ-1) in Slovenian; the summary is ours. It is guidance, not the statute text.

value: A dwelling is let by a written lease for a fixed or indefinite term. The lease must contain at least: description of the dwelling, owner and tenant details, termination grounds under Art. 103 SZ-1, type of rental category, amount of rent and how and when it is paid, how running costs are charged, and the duration if fixed-term.
source_publisher: Ministry of Natural Resources and Spatial Planning of Slovenia (PIS spatial information portal)
note: Official government guidance on the Housing Act (Stanovanjski zakon, SZ-1) in Slovenian; the summary is ours. It is guidance, not the statute text.

value: The owner must hand over the dwelling in a state allowing normal use, maintain the dwelling and common parts throughout the lease, and answer for legal and physical defects.
source_publisher: Ministry of Natural Resources and Spatial Planning of Slovenia (PIS spatial information portal)
note: Official government guidance on the Housing Act (Stanovanjski zakon, SZ-1) in Slovenian; the summary is ours. It is guidance, not the statute text.

value: Unless agreed otherwise, the tenant may terminate without giving reasons by written notice with a 60-day notice period.
source_publisher: Ministry of Natural Resources and Spatial Planning of Slovenia (PIS spatial information portal)
note: Official government guidance on the Housing Act (Stanovanjski zakon, SZ-1) in Slovenian; the summary is ours. It is guidance, not the statute text.

value: The owner terminates with a notice period of not less than 60 days and cannot demand the tenant move out before repaying the tenant's investments; disputes are decided by court action, and the court sets a move-out period of 30 to 60 days.
source_publisher: Ministry of Natural Resources and Spatial Planning of Slovenia (PIS spatial information portal)
note: Official government guidance on the Housing Act (Stanovanjski zakon, SZ-1) in Slovenian; the summary is ours. It is guidance, not the statute text.

value: The owner may terminate for fault-based grounds listed in Art. 103 SZ-1 (for example, rent or costs not paid within the contract deadline or, if none, within 60 days of receiving the invoice; unauthorised sub-letting; refusing entry). The tenant must first receive a written warning naming the breach and giving at least 15 days to remedy it; for the same breach the owner warns only once unless more than a year passes between two breaches.
source_publisher: Ministry of Natural Resources and Spatial Planning of Slovenia (PIS spatial information portal)
note: Official government guidance on the Housing Act (Stanovanjski zakon, SZ-1) in Slovenian; the summary is ours. It is guidance, not the statute text.

value: The tenant must allow the owner or representative to enter to check proper use, at most twice a year.
